opening: Srinagar, Nov 12: Jammu and Kashmir National Conference president Farooq Abdullah on Thursday called on Pakistan to end terrorism and choose dialogue to resolve outstanding issues, amid a spate of security incidents in Jammu and Kashmir, including the killing of two Special.
Police Officers (SPOs) in Kishtwar.
body: Abdullah said terrorism should not intimidate people and reiterated that Kashmir was, is and will always remain a part of India.
He also emphasised the need to revive the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) to facilitate dialogue and regional cooperation.
"Terrorism exists, but we must not be intimidated by it.
Kashmir was, is, and will always remain a part of India...
I have always told Pakistan: put an end to terrorism.
Terrorism will lead nowhere.
Choose the path of dialogue; that is the only way a solution can be found.
We were once part of the same nation...
We must revive SAARC so that we can all sit together, resolve our issues, and move toward progress," he said.

Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) MLA Aga Syed Muntazir Mehdi strongly condemned the attack on CRPF personnel in Kulgam on Wednesday and the killing of two SPOs in Kishtwar, while questioning the Central Government's approach towards Kashmir.
He said violence had no place in a civilised or democratic society and stressed that controlling the visible signs of instability could not be considered a permanent solution.
"We strongly condemn yesterday’s attack in Kulgam and the incident reported in Kishtwar today.
Violence has no place in a civilised or democratic society.
However, these repeated incidents raise serious questions about the Central Government’s approach towards Kashmir...
The government may have controlled the visible signs of instability, but control is not a permanent solution," Mehdi said.

In Kulgam district, a massive cordon and search operation (CASO) continued on Thursday after unidentified motorcycle-borne assailants opened fire on CRPF personnel deployed at a security checkpoint in Nowpora Akhran on Wednesday.
The attack took place at around 2:15 pm, when the assailants opened fire on the security personnel before fleeing the spot.
Three CRPF personnel sustained injuries in the firing and were shifted to a hospital in Anantnag district for treatment.

In another incident from Kishtwar, the bullet-riddled bodies of the two SPOs, identified as Babi Chand (57) and Rashpal Kumar (45), were recovered on Thursday morning, a day after they went missing in the remote Dachhan belt.
The two personnel were posted with the Special Operations Group (SOG) of the local police at Kiyar village in Dachhan.
They had gone missing on Wednesday while travelling from their camp towards an Army post at Dharna-Marwah.
Kishtwar MLA Shagun Parihar expressed grief over the killings, stating that the bodies of the two personnel were recovered at around 8 am and 9 am, respectively.
"Regarding the incident in which two SPOs (Special Police Officers) were reportedly killed—what are your thoughts?
It is a truly tragic incident.
Two of our SPOs from the southern region have been killed.
They had gone missing last night, and their bodies were recovered this morning—one around 8:00 AM and the other around 9:00 AM.
It is deeply saddening," Parihar said.

The tolerance zone of the RBI ranges from 2 per cent to 6 per cent.
The RBI's monetary policy aims to keep inflation within this zone as it balances its objective of promoting economic growth with stability.
The monetary policy committee voted unanimously to increase the policy repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5 per cent on October 7.

The latest reading represents a 55-basis-point increase over the previous month and takes inflation above the RBI’s upper tolerance limit of 6 per cent.
The central bank’s inflation-targeting framework mandates maintaining CPI inflation at 4 per cent, with a tolerance band of 2 per cent to 6 per cent.
Rural food inflation stood at 9.09 per cent, while urban food inflation was recorded at 8.68 per cent.
At the national level, inflation in the food and beverages category stood at 8.51 per cent.
Personal care, social protection and miscellaneous goods and services recorded inflation of 10.14 per cent, while restaurants and accommodation services saw a rise of 10.06 per cent.
Among individual food items, onion prices recorded inflation of 116.22 per cent in October, compared with 108.13 per cent in September.
Garlic inflation rose to 60.74 per cent from 54.62 per cent during the same period.
Rural inflation increased to 6.63 per cent in October from 6.08 per cent in September, while urban inflation rose to 5.41 per cent from 4.88 per cent.
The inflation reading comes after the RBI raised the policy repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50 per cent at its October policy review and shifted its stance to calibrated tightening.
The December 2-4 meeting will be the next opportunity for the MPC to assess the implications of rising price pressures for monetary policy.

stories.headline: Divorce allowed in foreign country cannot end marriage in India: Supreme Court
stories.title: Divorce allowed in foreign country cannot end marriage in India: Supreme Court
stories.summary: Divorce allowed in foreign country cannot end marriage in India: Supreme Court
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The court held that a foreign divorce decree must meet the conditions prescribed under Section 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC) before it can be recognised by Indian courts.

The Supreme Court has observed that a marriage solemnised in India cannot be automatically dissolved or stand null and void by a divorce order passed by a foreign court, reiterating that such judgments must satisfy the requirements of Indian law to be legally recognised in the country.

The top court also specifically held that a foreign divorce granted solely on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage cannot be treated as valid in India when the marriage was solemnised under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

A bench comprising Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar made the observation on Tuesday while dismissing a man's plea seeking quashing of criminal proceedings initiated against him for bigamy and criminal conspiracy.
"In our view, the foreign divorce decree was passed in contravention of the existing matrimonial law in India and on a ground that is not even recognised statutorily," the bench observed.
It further stated that the decree violated the legal requirements under Section 13 of the CPC, which every foreign judgment must satisfy to be enforceable in India.
The court emphasised that the validity of a marriage solemnised under Indian law cannot be determined solely on the basis of proceedings conducted in a foreign jurisdiction.
It also rejected the argument that the husband's subsequent foreign citizenship and divorce proceedings abroad could absolve him of liability under Indian law.
"We cannot accept this submission in the manner canvassed as accused No.1/husband was married to respondent No.2/first wife in India under the Hindu rites, rituals and customs," the bench said.

The court added that even if the second marriage took place outside India, the allegations under Section 494 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) could not be diluted, as an inquiry into bigamy must consider whether the first marriage continued to subsist.
The case concerned a man who married his first wife on April 18, 2003, in Sattenapalli, Andhra Pradesh, according to Hindu rites and customs.
The couple subsequently lived in Hyderabad, where the husband was pursuing his postgraduate studies at Osmania Medical College.

stories.title: India’s GDP growth seen at 7.7% in Q3 on strong manufacturing push
stories.summary: India’s economy is expected to remain robust in Q3 FY27, with GDP growth projected at 7.7% and GVA growth at 8.1%, driven by strong manufacturing, industrial activity, consumer demand and credit growth, despite global uncertainties and potential risks from oil prices and geopolitics.

article_sentences: India’s economy is expected to remain robust in Q3 FY27, with GDP growth projected at 7.7% and GVA growth at 8.1%, driven by strong manufacturing, industrial activity, consumer demand and credit growth, despite global uncertainties and potential risks from oil prices and geopolitics.

New Delhi: India’s GDP growth remains strong and is expected to reach 7.7 per cent year-on-year in the October-November period (Q3), with GVA growth estimated at 8.1 per cent, a report by BofA Global Research said on Thursday.
BofA maintains its full-year FY27 GDP growth forecast at 7.4 per cent, with modest upside risks, projecting 7.5 per cent growth for FY28.
The growth reflects resilient economic momentum despite global supply-side headwinds from the West Asia disruption, uneven monsoons, and weakness in the farm sector.
Strong industrial and manufacturing activity, along with sustained consumer demand and credit growth, is expected to support overall growth.
Manufacturing is expected to grow around 12 per cent, supported by stronger industrial activity, with IIP growth rising to 7.3 per cent in Q3 from 6.2 per cent in Q2, the report showed.
Auto sales, power demand, and freight activity remain strong, while bank credit growth continues at around 20 per cent.
“We expect the H1 FY27 GDP growth to now average at 7.7 per cent YoY, modestly lower than 8.1 per cent YoY in H2 FY26.
We continue to project GDP growth for the full year at 7.4 per cent YoY for FY27 but see modest upside risks to our GDP growth projections,” said the report.
The nominal GDP growth estimate for Q2 FY27 is around 13.9 per cent YoY, which will be the highest nominal growth print in almost four years.
“We expect the growth momentum to hold in the next fiscal year and keep our forecast unchanged for FY28 at 7.5 per cent YoY.
The growth momentum in India appears quite resilient, however, the downside risks to activity appear largely global in nature.

stories.headline: Technological superiority key to enhancing operational readiness against emerging threats: Rajanth Singh
stories.title: Technological superiority key to enhancing operational readiness against emerging threats: Rajanth Singh
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 12: Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has called upon the Defence Forces to strengthen and sustain both offensive and defensive dimensions of the ‘element of surprise’ to maintain operational readiness against conventional and emerging threats arising from rapid technological advancements and the evolving nature of modern warfare. Addressing the Air Force Commanders’ Conference in New Delhi on November 12, 2026, he emphasised the need to continue bolstering intelligence and surveillance capabilities, enhance integration among systems and identify potential threats before they unfold. “Our Defence Forces must develop capabilities and methods that leave the adversary with no time to react or recover, while simultaneously ensuring that we are never caught off guard by an unexpected move from the enemy. Surprise can manifest in various forms, both conventional and electronic. Our intelligence and surveillance mechanisms must be further strengthened and operational preparedness enhanced to ensure that our personnel remain alert, agile and equipped to respond effectively to any emerging challenge,” said the Raksha Mantri. Shri Rajnath Singh asserted that contemporary conflicts are extending beyond traditional battlefields into non-contact domains, with missiles, drones and advanced weapon systems playing a significant role. Referring to the Russia-Ukraine and Israel-Hamas conflicts, he stated that drones and air defence systems have emerged as critical components of modern warfare. He exhorted the Commanders to remain prepared for emerging challenges such as kamikaze drones, surveillance and counter-drone operations. Raksha Mantri called upon the Indian Air Force (IAF) to develop dedicated doctrines and architectures for emerging domains of warfare, including electronic, cyber and space. He emphasised that enhanced preparedness in these domains would strengthen the ability to address future challenges. “Victory in future conflicts would depend not merely on the number of aircraft, but also on technological sophistication, speed of response and precision of preparations,” he said, urging the Commanders to make these emerging challenges a core priority, with focus on integrating them into institutional thinking, planning and operational processes. Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted that the Defence Forces are undergoing a transformative phase, encompassing reforms in wide-ranging areas, including organisational structures, jointness & integration, and operational concepts. He added that the changing security environment necessitated continuous adaptation and a forward-looking approach to military preparedness. Raksha Mantri commended the IAF for effectively implementing its doctrines and operational methods during and after Operation Sindoor, appreciating the professionalism, restraint & judgement demonstrated by the air warriors in successfully executing their assigned tasks. He stated that the lessons learnt during the operation were clearly reflected in the IAF's evolving operational procedures, particularly through the increased emphasis on drones and air defence systems, which are vital to national security. These lessons, he added, are shaping the pace and direction of the transformative changes underway in the Defence Forces. Highlighting the coordinated and complementary contributions of all the three Services effectively demonstrated during Op Sindoor, Shri Rajnath Singh congratulated the Defence Forces for the synergy and integration. He underlined that jointness and integrated efforts must continue to guide military planning and operational execution. While appreciating the IAF for enhancing the skills and capabilities of its personnel in keeping with rapid technological advancements, Raksha Mantri urged the Commanders to sustain efforts towards training air warriors in emerging technologies. He underscored the importance of leveraging the technological knowledge and expertise of young recruits, stating that their capabilities could contribute significantly to stronger decision-making and organisational development. On the Second Tour of Duty for Agniveers, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that the decision was taken following feedback received from the Defence Forces, reiterating the Government's commitment to incorporating the Services’ suggestions into policy decisions. He expressed confidence that the ‘Second Tour of Duty’ initiative would contribute to further bolstering the three Services. As part of this conference, Raksha Mantri launched a suite of Artificial Intelligence (Al) applications developed in-house by the IAF's Al Centre of Excellence of the Unit for Digitisation, Automation, Artificial Intelligence and Application Networking (UDAAN). The applications will be utilised to automate and expedite tasks across the domains of operations, administration and aerospace safety, and are deployed on the IAF’s secure network. The initiative marks a significant milestone in the IAF's pursuit of technology-driven transformation and enhanced operational capabilities. The inaugural session was also attended by Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth, Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary (Defence Production) Shri Sanjeev Kumar, and Secretary (Defence Finance) Shri Vishvajit Sahay. Air Officers Commanding-in-Chief of all Commands of IAF, all Principal Staff Officers & all Director Generals. The two-day conference is being attended by the Air Officers Commanding-in-Chief of all Commands of IAF, all Principal Staff Officers & all Director Generals. The theme of this year’s conference is ‘The Year of Empowerment: Maximising Efficiency Through Decentralisation’. The conference provides a forum to the senior leadership of the IAF to discuss critical issues pertaining to operations, maintenance and administration.

Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted that the Defence Forces are undergoing a transformative phase, encompassing reforms in wide-ranging areas, including organisational structures, jointness & integration, and operational concepts.
He added that the changing security environment necessitated continuous adaptation and a forward-looking approach to military preparedness.

Raksha Mantri commended the IAF for effectively implementing its doctrines and operational methods during and after Operation Sindoor, appreciating the professionalism, restraint & judgement demonstrated by the air warriors in successfully executing their assigned tasks.

He stated that the lessons learnt during the operation were clearly reflected in the IAF's evolving operational procedures, particularly through the increased emphasis on drones and air defence systems, which are vital to national security.
These lessons, he added, are shaping the pace and direction of the transformative changes underway in the Defence Forces.

Highlighting the coordinated and complementary contributions of all the three Services effectively demonstrated during Op Sindoor, Shri Rajnath Singh congratulated the Defence Forces for the synergy and integration.
He underlined that jointness and integrated efforts must continue to guide military planning and operational execution.

While appreciating the IAF for enhancing the skills and capabilities of its personnel in keeping with rapid technological advancements, Raksha Mantri urged the Commanders to sustain efforts towards training air warriors in emerging technologies.

He underscored the importance of leveraging the technological knowledge and expertise of young recruits, stating that their capabilities could contribute significantly to stronger decision-making and organisational development.

On the Second Tour of Duty for Agniveers, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that the decision was taken following feedback received from the Defence Forces, reiterating the Government's commitment to incorporating the Services’ suggestions into policy decisions.
He expressed confidence that the ‘Second Tour of Duty’ initiative would contribute to further bolstering the three Services.

As part of this conference, Raksha Mantri launched a suite of Artificial Intelligence (Al) applications developed in-house by the IAF's Al Centre of Excellence of the Unit for Digitisation, Automation, Artificial Intelligence and Application Networking (UDAAN).
The applications will be utilised to automate and expedite tasks across the domains of operations, administration and aerospace safety, and are deployed on the IAF’s secure network.
The initiative marks a significant milestone in the IAF's pursuit of technology-driven transformation and enhanced operational capabilities.

The inaugural session was also attended by Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth, Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary (Defence Production) Shri Sanjeev Kumar, and Secretary (Defence Finance) Shri Vishvajit Sahay.
